paras: The threatened lynching of Tom Orchard and Wm. Tivris was an incident at Grain Valley, Jackson County, Missouri, shortly before 6 August 1881, in which a posse of citizens captured two men accused of the "inhuman treatment" of a woman, and the men "narrowly escaped lynching." They were jailed at Independence instead, and the case appeared only as a short item in a Missouri news column.

According to the only account, Orchard and a second man came to the house of James Keating at Grain Valley "the other night" while Mrs. Keating was alone. The two men were accused of subjecting her "to the most inhuman treatment"; the item gives no further detail of the charge. The race of the two men is not stated.

The men were later "captured by a posse of citizens," whose members and size were not reported. The item says they "narrowly escaped lynching" but does not say who wanted to lynch them, where the threat occurred, or what prevented it.
Both men were "lodged in jail at Independence." No report of an indictment, trial or later outcome was found in the coverage.

The story reached print as one paragraph in a "Miscellaneous Items" column of Missouri news, run by Fair Play of Ste. Genevieve on 6 August 1881 among accidents, suicides and crimes from St. Louis and Kansas City. The Iron County Register reprinted the same column on 11 August, unchanged except that the second man's name appeared as "Wm. Tivis" rather than "Win. Tivris." The item called the accused "Two scoundrels" and "The wretches," stated the accusation as fact, and reported the near-lynching without comment.
